plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-green narrow leaves and dense spikes of small, fragrant flowers. It is widely cultivated in gardens and commercial fields, and it is a magnet for bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Mediterranean region, southern France (Provence), England, and temperate gardens across North America
plants.funFact: Lavender oil has been used since Roman times for bathing and perfume, and the name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large composite flower head made of hundreds of tiny florets surrounded by bright yellow ray petals. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, and the plant produces edible seeds rich in oil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late summer (July to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated widely in Ukraine, Russia, Argentina, the United States, and Europe
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds follow the sun from east to west in a behavior called heliotropism, but mature blooms stay fixed facing east.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large round leaves that rise above the water and showy, fragrant flowers on tall stalks. The leaves have a water-repelling surface that keeps them clean, and the seeds and rhizomes are edible.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (June to August) in temperate Asia; nearly year-round in the tropics
plants.location: Ponds, lakes, and wetlands across India, China, Japan, Vietnam, and Southeast Asia, with naturalized populations in Australia
plants.funFact: Lotus seeds have been shown to germinate after more than 1,000 years of dormancy, and the flower can regulate its own temperature to attract pollinators.

plants.name: Eucalyptus caesia
plants.description: A small, graceful mallee-type eucalypt with weeping branches, powdery white-waxed bark and silvery-gray foliage. Its large pendulous flower clusters brighten the winter landscape and attract nectar-feeding birds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through winter and early spring (roughly May to September) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Granite outcrops of Western Australia, also grown in gardens in warm temperate regions
plants.funFact: This species grows naturally only on a handful of granite rock outcrops in Western Australia and is listed as a rare plant in the wild.
